candidates.evidence: Only one significant Raman line at 108.9 cm-1 with a weak shoulder near 143 cm-1, all below 150 cm-1. That fits a heavy-Te layered tellurosilicate (Si2Te6 units) with low-frequency Te-dominated modes. This is a family-level fit only. I have no reference spectrum for InSiTe3, so I cannot confirm the specific compound.

These tellurides have a strong Eg-type mode near 105-110 cm-1 and an A1g near 135-145 cm-1 (literature values from memory, not checked). The 109 and ~143 cm-1 lines are at similar positions. Their other lines (about 78, 90, 117, 200 cm-1) are not resolved here.

Te has modes near 92, 103 (E1), 121 (A1) and 141 (E2) cm-1. The weak 123 and 143 cm-1 features could match. However, the A1 mode near 121 cm-1 is normally dominant, and here it is nearly absent. The strong 109 cm-1 line does not fit Te well.
These have low-frequency Eg and A1g lines at about 100-115 and 135-165 cm-1, but a single dominant 109 cm-1 line with nothing else is not a good match.

limits: The spectrum has one confident Raman peak (108.9 cm-1) and one marginal peak (~143 cm-1). That is too little to identify the material uniquely. InSiTe3 is the best guess only because it is a Te-based layered compound with low-frequency modes. I could not check it against a reference spectrum.
Irreps and polarisation patterns cannot be determined. This is a single spectrum with no angle or parallel/crossed analysis, so the 'pattern' fields are null.
No Si substrate line near 520.7 cm-1 is seen, and the substrate is unknown. The sample may be thick or opaque, or the substrate may be something else.

The lines at 426.5 and 847.1 cm-1 are single-point spikes with a width of one sample point. They are cosmic rays, not sample peaks, and I excluded them. Ignoring them, there are no clear modes above about 150 cm-1. The ~764 and ~391 cm-1 features are noise-level.

Te-based and other heavy-chalcogenide layered materials give similar low-frequency lines, so the alternatives listed cannot be excluded. A wider low-wavenumber range (below 60 cm-1), higher S/N, polarisation data, and the substrate identity would be needed to decide.
Layer number, doping, strain and defect level cannot be determined from these data.
